2027-06-06.title: Third Sunday after Pentecost
readings: The Twelve sent out two by two
We will not worship the golden statue
Through this man forgiveness of sins is proclaimed
I am the bread of life
2027-06-06.verse: I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
theo: Jesus says: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty… Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away… This is indeed the will of my Father, that all who see the Son and believe in him may have eternal life; and I will raise them up on the last day.” And: “No one can come to me unless drawn by the Father who sent me.” Faith itself is a gift: the Father draws, the Spirit moves the heart.

In the evening Gospel Jesus is rejected in his own town: “Prophets are not without honor, except in their hometown, and among their own kin, and in their own house.” Yet he does not stop. He sends the Twelve two by two, with authority over unclean spirits. “So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.” The mission of the Church begins in weakness and is carried by the Spirit's power.

In the book of Daniel three young men stand before a golden statue and a blazing furnace. They say to the king: “If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.” This is faith that does not bargain: God first, whatever happens.

St Paul writes: “So then, whenever we have an opportunity, let us work for the good of all, and especially for those of the family of faith… May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ… a new creation is everything!” In Baptism we became a new creation; the bread of life keeps us alive as God's new people.
conn: Joseph's brothers.
Genesis 42: the brothers recognise their guilt; Jeremiah 3: “Return to me”; Acts 13:38: forgiveness proclaimed through Jesus.
The furnace.
Daniel 3: fidelity under threat; Galatians 6:14: boasting only in the Cross.
Anointing with oil.
Mark 6:13: the apostles anoint the sick; the Church sees here a hint of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick (James 5:14).
Bread in Egypt.
Joseph gives grain to his hungry brothers (Genesis 42:25); Jesus is the bread of life for the world.
altar: “I am the bread of life.” At the Holy Qurbono the Father draws us to the Son, and the Son gives himself to us, so that we may never hunger and may be raised on the last day.
outline: Rejected at home, yet sending others.
Come to Jesus; he will never drive you away.
Mission in weakness: repentance, healing, anointing.
The three young men: faith without bargaining.
Doing good to all, boasting only in the Cross.
“Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.”
live: Go two by two
Visit a sick or lonely person this week with a family member or friend.
Faith without bargaining
Tell God: “Even if you do not answer as I wish, I will trust you.”
Receive worthily
Prepare for Holy Qurbono with confession if needed.
fathers: St Augustine
“No one comes unless drawn.” You are drawn not by force but by delight; show a green branch to a sheep and you draw it; so Christ, revealed by the Father, draws us (Tractates on John 26, 4–5).
St Hippolytus of Rome
The three youths teach us that the faithful must prefer death to denying God, and God stood with them in the furnace (Commentary on Daniel II).
magis: Catechism 1406
“I am the living bread that came down from heaven; whoever eats of this bread will live for ever.”
Catechism 1511
The Church believes that a special sacrament for the sick was instituted by Christ, hinted at in Mark 6:13 and promulgated by James 5:14.
Catechism 2087–2089
Faith requires us to worship God alone and refuse all idols.
saints: 8 June: St Mariam Thresia. 11 June: Mar Barthulmai (Bartholomew) and Mar Barnabas, Apostles; anniversary of the erection of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Hierarchy (11 June 1932). 13 June: St Antony of Padua.
2027-06-06.prayer: Lord Jesus, bread of life, draw us to yourself and never drive us away. Make us faithful like the three young men in the furnace, send us two by two to heal and proclaim repentance, and make us a new creation for the good of all. Amen.

2027-06-20.title: Fifth Sunday after Pentecost
readings: Whoever wants to be first must be servant of all
Three times a year you shall keep a festival
I will be like the dew to Israel
Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength
Ananias and Saul: a chosen instrument
We are the temple of the living God
You give them something to eat
2027-06-20.alt: Season of Pentecost. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was Seminary Day, with the collection sent to the eparchial curia for the Seminary Fund. The Thirteen Days' Fast of the Apostles (Sleehanombu) is under way, ending on 29 June.
2027-06-20.verse: Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.
theo: In the Gospel the crowd is hungry and the day is ending. The disciples want to send them away. Jesus says: “You give them something to eat.” They have only five loaves and two fish. Jesus “taking the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, and blessed and broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd. And all ate and were filled.” What little we bring, Christ blesses and multiplies; but he gives it through the hands of his disciples. This is the priesthood: hands that receive from Christ and give to the people.

In the evening Gospel the disciples argue about who is the greatest. Jesus sits down, calls the Twelve and says: “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.” Then he takes a little child in his arms: “Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.” The Church does not need ambitious men but servants.

In Acts the Lord sends Ananias to Saul, the persecutor: “Go, for he is an instrument whom I have chosen to bring my name before Gentiles and kings and before the people of Israel.” Ananias lays hands on him, and Saul is filled with the Holy Spirit. God calls unexpected people, and he uses other people's hands to form them. Seminaries exist for this: so that those whom God chooses may be formed to serve.

Isaiah encourages the weary: “He gives power to the faint… those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary.” Priests and seminarians, catechists and parents grow tired. The Spirit renews those who wait on the Lord.
conn: Bread in the wilderness.
The feeding of the five thousand recalls the manna and points to the Eucharist: “blessed and broke them, and gave them to the disciples.”
Festival and first fruits.
Exodus 23: Israel offers the first fruits; the Church offers her sons and daughters to God's service.
Chosen instrument.
Acts 9:15: Saul the persecutor becomes Paul the apostle.
Temple of the living God.
2 Corinthians 6:16: we are God's temple; holiness of life is the soil of vocations.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the priest does what the disciples did: he receives the bread blessed and broken by Christ and gives it to the people. Pray today for priests and for those preparing to be priests.
outline: Five loaves, two fish, and a hungry crowd.
Point 1 · You give them something to eat
God calls and forms: Ananias, Saul, the seminary.
Renewed strength for those who serve.
“Whoever wants to be first must be servant of all.”
live: Pray for a seminarian
Pray each day this week for the seminarians of your eparchy, by name if you know one.
Bring your five loaves
Offer your time or talent to your parish, however small.
Serve without being seen
Do one service at home that no one asks for.
fathers: St Ambrose
He gave the loaves to the disciples to distribute, as he gives the Bread of heaven through the ministry of the Church (Exposition of Luke 6, 84–86).
St Gregory the Great
The pastor must be a servant first; he who seeks to rule rather than to serve is not a shepherd (Pastoral Rule I).
magis: Catechism 1335
The miracles of the multiplication of the loaves prefigure the superabundance of the Eucharist.
Catechism 1548
In the ministry of the priest it is Christ himself who is present to his Church as Head and Shepherd.
Optatam Totius 2
The duty of fostering vocations falls on the whole Christian community, especially families.
saints: 24 June: Birth of St John the Baptist. 29 June (Tue): Sts Peter and Paul, end of the Thirteen Days' Fast.
2027-06-20.prayer: Lord Jesus, you took the five loaves, blessed and broke them, and gave them to your disciples for the crowd. Bless our seminarians and priests; make them servants of all; renew the strength of all who are weary in your service, and send labourers into your harvest. Amen.

2027-06-27.title: Sixth Sunday after Pentecost
readings: Increase our faith; we are worthless slaves
Some take pride in chariots, but our pride is in the name of the Lord
Paul at the Areopagus: in him we live and move
2027-06-27.alt: Season of Pentecost. In the 2025–26 lectionary the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost was Family Day and the commemoration of the Seventy-two Disciples. The Thirteen Days' Fast ends on Tuesday 29 June (Sts Peter and Paul).
2027-06-27.verse: Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
theo: Jesus tells of a shepherd with a hundred sheep who loses one. He leaves the ninety-nine and goes after the lost one “until he finds it. When he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders and rejoices.” And he calls his friends: “Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.” God is not a cold judge counting sins; he is a shepherd who searches and carries. “There will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.”

St Paul tells the Corinthians that the Church is a body: “For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ… If one member suffers, all suffer together with it; if one member is honoured, all rejoice together with it.” The family is the first place where we learn this: every member matters, the weakest most of all.

In the evening Gospel Jesus says hard things about forgiveness: “If the same person sins against you seven times a day, and turns back to you seven times and says, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive.” The apostles cry out: “Increase our faith!” Forgiving again and again needs faith that God is greater than our hurt. And Jesus adds: when you have done everything, say, “We are worthless slaves; we have done only what we ought to have done.” No pride, only humble service.

At the Areopagus Paul tells the philosophers of Athens about the unknown God: “he is not far from each one of us. For ‘In him we live and move and have our being.’” God is near every person, searching for them like the shepherd. Our homes should be places where the lost are welcomed back and where God's nearness is felt.
conn: The shepherd king.
2 Samuel 3: Israel is brought together under David the shepherd; Christ the Good Shepherd gathers the lost.
Incense.
Exodus 30: the holy incense rises before God; in the Qurbono incense rises with our prayers and the prayers of the Church.
The Lord's name.
Psalm 20:7: “our pride is in the name of the LORD our God”; Luke 17:10: we are only servants.
One body.
1 Corinthians 12 and Luke 15: no one in the body or the flock is expendable.
altar: The incense that rises at the Holy Qurbono recalls the holy incense of Exodus 30 and the prayers of the saints (Revelation 8:4). Christ the Shepherd, who carried the lost sheep, carries us to the Father in this sacrifice.
outline: Joy in heaven over one sinner.
Every member counts, especially the weak.
In him we live and move.
“Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.”
live: Bring back one
Call or visit someone in your family or parish who has drifted from the Church.
Family prayer
Pray together as a family every evening this week, even briefly.
Forgive again
Forgive one repeated hurt and ask for more faith.
fathers: St Gregory the Great
The shepherd lays the sheep on his shoulders, for Christ took our human nature upon himself and carried our sins (Homilies on the Gospels 34).
St John Chrysostom
Make your house a church; let the father and mother be like priests teaching the household (Homilies on Genesis 2, 4).
magis: Catechism 1443
Jesus' welcome of sinners shows the reconciliation of the sinner with God and the Church.
Catechism 1655–1657
The Christian family is a domestic church, where the faith is first proclaimed.
Catechism 791
The unity of the Mystical Body: when one member suffers, all suffer.
saints: 29 June (Tue): Sts Peter and Paul, Apostles; Holy Qurbono for the people; end of the Thirteen Days' Fast. 3 July (Sat): Dukrono of St Thomas the Apostle.
2027-06-27.prayer: Good Shepherd, you leave the ninety-nine to seek the one who is lost. Seek us when we stray and carry us home on your shoulders. Make our families one body in you, increase our faith to forgive again and again, and let heaven rejoice over every sinner who returns. Amen.

2027-06-29.title: Sts Peter and Paul, Apostles
readings: You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church
Daniel resolves not to defile himself
I have called you by name, you are mine
An angel frees Peter from prison
I have fought the good fight
2027-06-29.alt: Feast of Sts Peter and Paul: Holy Qurbono for the people. End of the Thirteen Days' Fast (Sleehanombu).
2027-06-29.verse: And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
theo: At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asks: “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answers: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.” Jesus replies: “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father in heaven. And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven.” The Church rests on the faith Peter confessed and on the office Christ gave him, continued in the Bishop of Rome.

After the Resurrection, by the lake, Jesus asks Peter three times: “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Three times Peter had denied him; three times he now confesses his love; three times Jesus entrusts him: “Feed my lambs… Tend my sheep… Feed my sheep.” Peter's authority is born from mercy and love, and it ends in martyrdom: “someone else will fasten a belt around you and take you where you do not wish to go.”

Paul writes from prison near the end of his life: “I am already being poured out as a libation, and the time of my departure has come. I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.” The persecutor became the apostle of the nations; the fisherman became the rock. Both gave their lives in Rome under Nero, and the Church of Rome is built on their blood.

In Acts, Peter sleeps in prison between two soldiers, and “the church prayed fervently to God for him.” An angel comes, the chains fall from his hands. Today we pray for Peter's successor, Pope Leo XIV, and for our Major Archbishop, in communion with him. The Syro-Malankara Church entered this communion in 1930 precisely to be united with the see of Peter.
conn: Abram called.
Genesis 12: Abram leaves his land at God's word; Peter leaves his nets, Paul his former life.
Called by name.
Isaiah 43:1: “I have called you by name, you are mine”; Simon receives a new name, Peter; Saul becomes Paul.
Daniel's fidelity.
Daniel 1: faithful in a foreign court; Peter and Paul faithful unto death in Rome.
The keys.
Isaiah 22:22: the key of the house of David; Matthew 16:19: the keys of the kingdom.
altar: In every Holy Qurbono of our Church the Pope of Rome is commemorated in the diptychs together with our Major Archbishop and bishop: a sign that we offer the one sacrifice in communion with Peter.
outline: Two very different men, one faith, one martyrdom.
The rock and the keys: the ministry of unity.
Point 3 · I have kept the faith
Point 4 · The Church prayed for him
Our prayer for the Pope and our bishops.
“Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.”
live: Pray for the Pope
Pray an Our Father and Hail Mary for Pope Leo XIV and our Major Archbishop today.
Answer Jesus
Tell Jesus three times in prayer: “Lord, you know that I love you.”
Keep the faith
Ask Sts Peter and Paul for courage to keep the faith in a hard situation.
fathers: St Augustine
One day is kept for the passion of both apostles, but they were one; though they suffered on different days, they were one (Sermon 295).
St Leo the Great
Peter and Paul are the two eyes of the body whose head is Christ; through them the Gospel shone on Rome (Sermon 82).
magis: Catechism 881–882
The Lord made Simon alone the rock of his Church; the Pope, Peter's successor, is the perpetual and visible source of unity.
Catechism 553
The power of the keys: authority to govern the house of God.
Lumen Gentium 22
The college of bishops with Peter's successor as its head.
saints: 3 July (Sat): Dukrono of St Thomas the Apostle; Holy Qurbono for the people.
2027-06-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, you built your Church on the rock of Peter's faith and spread your Gospel through Paul's labours. By their prayers keep us faithful to the end; protect Pope Leo, our Major Archbishop and our bishops; and give us hearts that answer you each day: “Lord, you know that I love you.” Amen.

2027-06-13.title: Fourth Sunday after Pentecost
readings: The Lord sends out the seventy
Moses blesses the tribes of Israel
The Lord has given you the city
Who may abide in your tent?
There is a blessing in the cluster
Seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom
Rejoice that your names are written in heaven
2027-06-13.alt: Season of Pentecost. St Antony of Padua. The Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) runs from Wednesday 16 June to Tuesday 29 June, the feast of Sts Peter and Paul: remind the faithful today.
2027-06-13.verse: Nevertheless, do not rejoice at this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.
theo: In the evening Gospel the Lord appoints seventy others and sends them ahead of him in pairs to every town he means to visit. Before he gives them any instruction about what to do, he tells them what to pray for: “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.” Mission begins on our knees. The harvest belongs to the Lord, and so do the laborers.

Then comes a strange commission: “See, I am sending you out like lambs into the midst of wolves.” No purse, no bag, no sandals. They are to enter a house and say first, “Peace to this house!” They heal the sick and announce that the kingdom of God has come near. The messenger carries so little so that the message may be seen clearly: the power is God's, not ours. And the Lord binds himself to these poor messengers: “Whoever listens to you listens to me.”

In the Gospel of the Qurbono the seventy come back full of joy: “Lord, in your name even the demons submit to us!” Jesus answers, “I watched Satan fall from heaven like a flash of lightning.” Yet he turns their joy to a deeper source: do not rejoice that spirits submit to you, “but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.” Success in ministry passes; belonging to God remains. A catechist, a choir member, a priest, a parent who prays with the children: the deepest joy of each is not what they achieve but that God knows them by name.

The other readings fill out the picture. At Jericho the walls fall not by siege engines but by obedience, procession and the sound of the priests' trumpets: “the LORD has given you the city.” In Acts the apostles hand the daily service of the tables to seven men “full of the Spirit and of wisdom” so that they may give themselves to prayer and to serving the word, and “the word of God continued to spread.” St Paul reminds the Corinthians that the cup we bless and the bread we break are a sharing in the Blood and Body of Christ; because there is one bread, we who are many are one body. The Church is sent out from the altar.
conn: Seventy or seventy-two?

Ancient manuscripts of Luke differ: some read seventy, some seventy-two (the NRSV prints seventy, the POC seventy-two). In Genesis 10 the nations of the earth number seventy in the Hebrew text and seventy-two in the Greek: the mission of the seventy points to all the nations.
Moses' last blessing.

Deuteronomy 33 is Moses' farewell blessing on the tribes before his death. It ends: “Happy are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD.” The seventy are sent to share that blessing with every town.
Seven times round Jericho.

Joshua 6: the priests carry the ark and blow the trumpets; on the seventh day, after the seventh circuit, the walls fall. The victory belongs to the Lord, as the seventy learn when the demons submit “in your name”.
A blessing in the cluster.
Isaiah 65:8: as the vinedresser spares a cluster because there is still good wine in it, God spares his servants. The Lord of the harvest sees what is good in a people before he sees what is wrong.
altar: “The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?” At the end of the Holy Qurbono we are sent out, as the seventy were, to carry the peace we have received at the altar into our houses and streets.
outline: Pray before you go: the harvest is the Lord's.
Point 1 · Ask the Lord of the harvest
Peace to this house; the power is God's.
Point 3 · Servants of the word and of the table
The seven in Acts; every ministry in the parish.
Point 4 · Rejoice that your names are written in heaven
The deepest joy is belonging to God.
“Rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
live: Pray for laborers
Each day this week pray for one priest, one religious and one young person who may be called (Luke 10:2).
Say “Peace to this house”
When you enter a home this week, bless it silently with the words of Luke 10:5.
Prepare for the Apostles' Fast
Decide today how you will keep the Shleeha Nombu from 16 June (Acts 6:4: prayer and the word).
fathers: St Gregory the Great
The world is full of priests, he lamented, yet in God's harvest a true laborer is rarely found; we take up the office but do not do its work (Homilies on the Gospels 17).
St Augustine
Speaking of 1 Corinthians 10:17 to the newly baptised: be what you see, and receive what you are, the Body of Christ (Sermon 272).
magis: Catechism 1396
The unity of the Mystical Body: the Eucharist makes the Church (quoting 1 Corinthians 10:16–17).
Catechism 849–851
The missionary mandate: the Church is sent by Christ to all nations, urged on by the love of God.
Evangelii Gaudium 120 (Pope Francis)
Every baptised person is a missionary disciple; we no longer say that we are “disciples” and “missionaries”, but always “missionary disciples”.
saints: 13 June: St Antony of Padua. 14 June: the prophet Elisha. 15 June: memory of the first church built in honour of the Mother of God. 16 June (Wed): the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) begins. 18 June: Mar Aprem Malpan (St Ephrem). 19 June: Mar Jude Thaddeus, Apostle.
2027-06-13.prayer: Lord of the harvest, you sent the seventy ahead of you in poverty and peace. Send laborers into your harvest today: priests, religious, catechists and families who announce your kingdom. Make us one body through the one bread we share, give us your peace to carry into every house, and let our deepest joy be that our names are written in heaven. Amen.

quick: “I am the bread of life”: whoever comes to Jesus will never hunger.
The Twelve are sent two by two to preach repentance and heal.
“But if not”: faith that will not worship idols whatever happens.
2027-06-06.action: Visit a sick or lonely person this week with someone from your family.
2027-06-06.question: Do I trust God even when he does not answer as I want?
2027-06-06.special: Third Sunday after Pentecost. This week (11 June): anniversary of the erection of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Hierarchy in 1932.
illus: In 1930 Mar Ivanios and a few companions entered communion with the Catholic Church, leaving buildings and properties behind. They had little, but went out like the apostles, two by two. In 1932 the Syro-Malankara hierarchy was erected. Faith first, whatever it costs.

family.explain: Three young men would not bow down to a golden statue, even when the king threatened them with fire. They loved God more than anything!
family.intention: We pray for courage to put God first always.
family.ask: Ask: “What ‘golden statues’ tempt us to put them before God?”

kidsaint: A Franciscan priest who preached so well that people said even the fish came to listen! He loved the poor, and people still give “St Antony's bread” to the hungry. Lesson: share your bread as Jesus shares himself.
term: Jesus sent the apostles in pairs (Mark 6:7; Luke 10:1): for support, for witness (two witnesses make a testimony), and as a sign that mission is done in communion, not alone.
termMore: On 11 June 1932 Pope Pius XI, by the bull Christo Pastorum Principi, erected the Syro-Malankara hierarchy with the Archeparchy of Trivandrum and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla. In 2005 the Church was raised to a Major Archiepiscopal Church.

quick: “You give them something to eat”: Christ feeds his people through his disciples.
“Whoever wants to be first must be servant of all.”
God chooses unexpected instruments and forms them for service.
2027-06-20.action: Pray each day this week for the seminarians of your eparchy.
2027-06-20.question: What are my “five loaves” that Jesus wants me to offer?
2027-06-20.special: Fifth Sunday after Pentecost. (In 2025–26: Seminary Day; collection for the Seminary Fund. Check your eparchy's circular.) Thirteen Days' Fast of the Apostles under way.
illus: A Kerala mother packs a tiffin of rice and fish for her son leaving for the seminary. Years later he holds up the Bread of Life at the altar. Her small gift became part of something far greater.

family.explain: A boy's small lunch of five loaves and two fish fed thousands when Jesus blessed it. When we give what we have, Jesus can do great things.
family.intention: We pray for priests and seminarians.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can we give to Jesus this week?”

catechism: The multiplication of loaves and the Eucharist.
The priest acts in the person of Christ.
kidsaint: A priest who found studying very hard and almost failed the seminary. But he loved God so much that people came from all over France to confess to him in the little village of Ars. He is patron of parish priests. Lesson: God can use anyone who loves him.
term: The Thirteen Days' Fast of the Apostles, kept in the Syro-Malankara Church before the feast of Sts Peter and Paul (29 June). It prepares the faithful to honour the apostles, the foundation of the Church.
termMore: A “seed-bed” (Latin seminarium) where candidates for the priesthood are formed in prayer, study, community life and pastoral service. St Mary's Malankara Major Seminary, Trivandrum, was established in 1989.

quick: The Good Shepherd searches for the lost one; heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.
The Church and the family are one body: every member matters.
Forgive seven times a day, and pray “Increase our faith!”
2027-06-27.action: Contact someone in your family or parish who has drifted from the Church.
2027-06-27.question: Who is the “lost sheep” God is asking me to seek?
2027-06-27.special: Sixth Sunday after Pentecost. (In 2025–26: Family Day and the Seventy-two Disciples. Check your eparchy's circular.) The Thirteen Days' Fast ends on Tuesday.
illus: A Kerala grandmother lit the evening lamp every day for a grandson who had stopped coming to church, and prayed the Rosary for him. Years later he came back for her funeral and stayed. The shepherd had been searching through her.

family.explain: Jesus is like a shepherd who goes looking for one lost sheep, and is so happy when he finds it that he carries it home on his shoulders.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family welcome someone who feels left out?”

kidsaint: A watchmaker and a lace-maker in France who prayed together with their five daughters every day. One of them became St Thérèse of the Child Jesus. They were canonised together in 2015. Lesson: a family that prays together grows saints.
term: Besides the Twelve, Jesus sent seventy-two others ahead of him two by two (Luke 10:1). The Syriac tradition honours them on a Sunday after Pentecost as the wider circle of missionaries.
termMore: Holy incense (Exodus 30:34–38) is used abundantly in the West Syriac liturgy. Its sweet smoke rising symbolises prayer ascending to God (Psalm 141:2) and the fragrance of Christ's sacrifice.

quick: “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church.”
“Do you love me?… Feed my sheep”: authority born of mercy and love.
“I have fought the good fight… I have kept the faith.”
2027-06-29.action: Pray today for Pope Leo XIV and our Major Archbishop.
2027-06-29.question: If Jesus asked me “Do you love me?”, what would my life answer?
2027-06-29.special: Sts Peter and Paul (Tuesday): Holy Qurbono for the people; end of the Thirteen Days' Fast.
illus: In Rome, under the high altar of St Peter's Basilica, archaeologists found the grave of a man venerated since the first century. Pope Paul VI announced in 1968 that the relics of St Peter had been identified. The Church is literally built on the fisherman.

family.explain: Peter had said three times that he did not know Jesus. Jesus forgave him by asking three times: “Do you love me?” Then he made Peter the shepherd of his people.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, our bishops and priests.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show Jesus that we love him this week?”

kidsaint: Peter was a fisherman who sometimes got things wrong, but he loved Jesus. Paul once fought against Christians, but Jesus changed his heart. Both became great apostles and gave their lives for Jesus in Rome. Lesson: Jesus can change anyone who says yes to him.
term: The special office Christ gave to Peter as the rock of the Church, the holder of the keys and the shepherd of the flock (Matthew 16; John 21), continued in the Bishop of Rome. The Catholic Eastern Churches, including the Syro-Malankara Church, are in full communion with him.
termMore: The Thirteen Days' Fast of the Apostles concludes on this feast. Fasting prepares us to honour the apostles who handed on the faith we received.

quick: Before sending the seventy, Jesus asks them to pray for laborers.
“Peace to this house!”: the first word of the messenger.
“Rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
2027-06-13.action: Pray each day this week for one priest and for one young person who may be called.
2027-06-13.question: Is my joy in what I achieve for God, or in belonging to him?
2027-06-13.special: Fourth Sunday after Pentecost. St Antony of Padua. Announce the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu), 16–29 June.
illus: An old catechist in a hill parish taught Sunday school for forty years. Few of his pupils remembered his lessons word for word. But when one of them was ordained a priest, the first person he blessed after his parents was the old man, who wept and said: “I only prayed and taught. The Lord of the harvest did the rest.”

family.explain: Jesus sent his friends in pairs to visit towns. They were to say “Peace to this house!”, heal the sick and tell people that God's kingdom was near.
family.intention: We pray for priests, sisters and catechists, and for new vocations from our parish.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family bring peace to a house we visit this week?”

kidsaint: Born in Lisbon in Portugal, he first became an Augustinian canon. When he saw the bodies of Franciscan friars martyred in Morocco brought home, he joined the Franciscans and wanted to be a missionary. God led him instead to preach in Italy and France, and crowds came to hear him. He died near Padua in 1231 and is a Doctor of the Church. Lesson: go where God sends you, and speak his word with love.
term: The Apostles' Fast. In the Syro-Malankara Church it is kept from 16 June to 29 June, ending with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul. The faithful pray, fast and give alms, asking for the apostolic spirit.
termMore: A number of fullness in the Bible: seventy elders shared the spirit of Moses (Numbers 11:16–25), and the list of nations in Genesis 10 has seventy (seventy-two in the Greek). The seventy disciples stand for the mission to every nation.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus went to his own town and was rejected. “Prophets are not without honor, except in their hometown.” Did he give up? No. He called the Twelve and sent them out two by two. They preached repentance, cast out demons, and anointed the sick with oil. The mission of the Church began with rejection, and went on in the power of God.

In the Gospel of John Jesus says: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry… anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.” What a promise! No sinner who comes to him is turned away. And he says: “No one can come to me unless drawn by the Father.” If you are here today, the Father has drawn you.

In the book of Daniel three young men refuse to worship the golden statue. They say: our God can save us from the fire; “but if not,” we still will not worship your gods. This is mature faith. It does not say “God, if you give me this, I will believe.” It says “God, whatever happens, I belong to you.” Our Malankara Church, born in 1930 with Mar Ivanios, knows this faith: they left property and buildings, but kept communion.

St Paul says: let us do good to all, and boast only in the Cross; what matters is a new creation. This week, go two by two: visit a sick or lonely person with someone from your family. And come often to the bread of life. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus sent his friends out two by two, like partners, to tell people about God and to help sick people.
In the Bible, three brave young men would not bow to a golden statue, even when the king was angry. They loved God more than anything!
Jesus says: “I am the bread of life.” Who can you visit this week with your mum, dad or friend?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the day is ending, the crowd is hungry, and the disciples want to send them away. Jesus says: “You give them something to eat.” They have only five loaves and two fish. Jesus takes them, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks, and gives them to the disciples to give to the people. All eat and are satisfied, and twelve baskets are left over.

Notice: Jesus does not drop bread from the sky. He feeds the crowd through the hands of his disciples. That is the mystery of the priesthood. At every Holy Qurbono a man takes bread, and Christ through his hands feeds his people. Today we pray for those hands: our priests, and the young men in our seminaries.

But the disciples also had to learn. In the evening Gospel they argued about who was the greatest. Jesus took a child in his arms and said: “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.” A priest, a parent, a leader is great only by serving.

God chooses surprising people. He chose Saul, the persecutor, and sent Ananias to lay hands on him. He may be choosing a boy or girl in your family. Do not say “not my son, not my daughter.” Offer your five loaves. And to all who are weary in service, Isaiah says: “Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles.” Amen.
kids: Children, a boy had five little loaves and two fish. He gave them to Jesus, and Jesus fed five thousand people!
Jesus gave the bread to his friends to share. Today priests share the Bread of Jesus with us at the Holy Qurbono.
Let's pray for priests and for boys who are learning to become priests. And what small thing will you give to Jesus?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus tells of a shepherd who has a hundred sheep and loses one. Ninety-nine are safe; why bother about one? But he leaves them and searches until he finds it. Then he lays it on his shoulders, joyful, and calls his friends: “Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.” That is how God looks at each of us. Not as a number, but as the one he is searching for.

St Paul says the Church is a body. “If one member suffers, all suffer together with it; if one member is honoured, all rejoice.” Our families are the first place we learn this. In a good family no one is left behind, not the sick grandparent, not the child who struggles in school, not the son or daughter who has wandered away.

In the evening Gospel Jesus asks something very hard: forgive your brother seven times in a day if he repents. The apostles cry out: “Increase our faith!” We cannot forgive like that by our own strength. We need faith that God is bigger than our hurt. And when we have done all this, Jesus says, we should say humbly: “We have done only what we ought to have done.”

Paul tells the Athenians: God “is not far from each one of us; in him we live and move and have our being.” Who is the lost sheep in your family, your street, your parish? Call them this week. Pray for them. Light the lamp for them in the evening. And let heaven rejoice. Amen.
kids: Children, a shepherd had a hundred sheep. One got lost! Did he say, “Never mind, I still have ninety-nine”? No! He searched and searched until he found it.
Then he carried it home on his shoulders and had a party! Jesus loves each of us like that.
Is there someone who feels left out in your class or family? How can you help them feel loved?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we honour two very different men. Peter, a fisherman from Galilee, impulsive and warm-hearted, who denied Jesus three times. Paul, an educated Pharisee, who persecuted the Church. Christ chose both, changed both, and both gave their lives in Rome.

At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asked: “Who do you say that I am?” Peter answered: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.” And Jesus said: “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom.” This is why we love and obey the Pope, Peter's successor. Our Malankara Church came into Catholic communion in 1930 precisely to be one with Peter.

But see how Peter's authority was born. After his denial, Jesus asked him three times: “Do you love me?” Peter answered: “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” And Jesus said: “Feed my sheep.” Authority in the Church is born from mercy and is exercised in love. A pope, a bishop, a priest, a parent: first love Jesus, then feed his sheep.

Paul, near his death, wrote: “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.” May each of us say that at the end of our life. Today, let us pray for Pope Leo, our Major Archbishop and our bishop, as the Church prayed fervently for Peter in prison. Sts Peter and Paul, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Peter was a fisherman. Jesus called him the Rock and made him the leader of the apostles. Today the Pope takes Peter's place!
Paul once hurt Christians, but Jesus met him and changed his heart. He travelled all over the world telling people about Jesus.
Jesus asked Peter: “Do you love me?” What would you answer? Let's say together: “Jesus, I love you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, before Jesus sent out the seventy, he did not give them money or maps. He gave them a prayer: “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.” Every vocation in the Church begins with someone praying. Somebody prayed for the priest who baptised you. Somebody is praying today for the priest who will one day anoint you.

Then Jesus said: “See, I am sending you out like lambs into the midst of wolves.” No purse, no bag, no sandals. They were to enter a house and first say, “Peace to this house!” Why so poor? So that people would see that the peace and the healing come from God, not from the messenger. Jericho fell not by weapons but by prayer and obedience. The Church grows the same way.

In Acts the apostles chose seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom to serve the tables, so that the apostles could give themselves to prayer and to the word. Every service in the parish matters: the one who teaches catechism, the one who cleans the church, the one who visits the sick. All of it is the work of the harvest. And all of it flows from the altar, where the one bread makes us one body.

The seventy came back rejoicing: even the demons obey us! Jesus said: rejoice rather that your names are written in heaven. Successes come and go; our name in the heart of God remains. This week, pray every day for vocations, bless the houses you enter with the peace of Christ, and prepare for the Apostles' Fast that begins on Wednesday. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus sent seventy friends to visit many towns. He told them to take no bag and no money, only his peace.
When they entered a house they said: “Peace to this house!” You can say that too, quietly in your heart, when you go into a house.
The friends came back very happy. Jesus said: be happy most of all because God knows your name in heaven. He knows your name too!

intro: Theme: “Sent two by two, fed by the Bread of Life.”
Rejected in his hometown, Jesus does not stop; he sends the Twelve two by two. In John he says: “I am the bread of life.” The three young men in Daniel show the courage of faith that refuses idols.

points.h: Come to the Bread of Life
sub: Isaiah invites the thirsty and the poor to come and eat freely.
Jesus says: whoever comes to me will never hunger; I will never drive away anyone who comes.
In the Holy Qurbono that invitation is fulfilled.
q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat!
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.”
points.apply: Prepare well for your next Holy Communion with a few minutes of silent prayer.

sub: “Two are better than one”: mission is done in communion, not alone.
Jesus sends the Twelve with authority; they preach repentance, cast out demons and anoint the sick.
The Church sees here a hint of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.
q: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they fall, one will lift up the other.
So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.
points.apply: Visit a sick or lonely person this week with a family member or friend.

points.h: Faith that will not bow to idols
sub: The three young men: “Our God is able to deliver us … but if not, we will not serve your gods.”
Mature faith does not bargain with God.
St Paul boasts only in the Cross, and in being a new creation.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire … let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.
May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
points.apply: Name one modern “golden statue” (money, status, screens) and refuse to bow to it this week.

concl: Fed by Christ, sent together, faithful to the end: this is the Church after Pentecost.
Let us come to the Bread of Life and go out to share it.
2027-06-06.resolve: Pray for the Syro-Malankara Church on the anniversary of its hierarchy (11 June 1932).

intro: Theme: “You give them something to eat.”

Jesus feeds the crowd through the hands of his disciples, teaches them that greatness is service, and calls unexpected instruments like Saul. This Sunday we pray especially for priests and seminarians.

sub: Through Elijah God kept the widow's jar of meal and jug of oil from running out.
Jesus blesses and breaks five loaves and gives them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
Every priest at the altar continues this: Christ feeds his people through human hands.
q: The jar of meal was not emptied, neither did the jug of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by Elijah.
And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, and blessed and broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd. And all ate and were filled.
points.apply: Pray by name for the priests who serve your parish.

sub: God told Jeremiah: before you were born I consecrated you.
He chose Saul, a persecutor, as his instrument, and sent Ananias to lay hands on him.
Vocations are God's gift and the Church's task: families and seminaries form those he calls.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
But the Lord said to him, “Go, for he is an instrument whom I have chosen to bring my name before Gentiles and kings and before the people of Israel.”
points.apply: Encourage a young person to consider whether God is calling them.

points.h: Servant of all, renewed in strength
sub: The disciples argue about greatness; Jesus places a child in their midst.
“Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
Those who serve grow weary; God gives power to the faint.
q: Those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
He sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
points.apply: Serve someone at home this week without being asked.

concl: Christ multiplies what we give and feeds the world through servants.
Let us pray for our priests, offer our five loaves, and serve with joy.
2027-06-20.resolve: Offer a day of prayer and fasting this week for seminarians.

intro: Theme: “The Shepherd who searches, the body that belongs together.”
Jesus tells of the shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine to find the one lost sheep. Paul reminds us that we are many members of one body. The apostles pray: “Increase our faith.”

points.h: The Shepherd searches for the lost
sub: Through Ezekiel God promised to seek the lost himself.
Jesus fulfils it: he goes after the one sheep until he finds it and carries it home on his shoulders.
Heaven rejoices more over one sinner who repents; the Sacrament of Reconciliation is that joy today.
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak.

Which one of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it? When he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders and rejoices.
points.apply: Pray for one person who has drifted from the Church, and reach out to them gently.

sub: Paul: the body is one though its members are many; no member can say “I have no need of you.”
The weaker members are indispensable; when one suffers, all suffer.
Family and parish are where this unity is lived first.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Now the whole group of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one claimed private ownership of any possessions, but everything they owned was held in common.
points.apply: Thank a family member or parishioner whose quiet service is often unnoticed.

sub: God's plans stand firm; nothing can overturn them.
Faith the size of a mustard seed is enough, because its power is God's.
Having done all, we say: “We are worthless slaves; we have done only what we ought to have done.” Humility guards faith.
q: The LORD of hosts has sworn: As I have designed, so shall it be; and as I have planned, so shall it come to pass.

The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!” The Lord replied, “If you had faith the size of a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.”
points.apply: Each day this week pray the apostles' prayer: “Lord, increase my faith.”

concl: The Shepherd seeks us, the body holds us, and faith keeps us humble and strong.
Let us return to him, belong to one another, and serve without seeking reward.
2027-06-27.resolve: Make a good confession before the feast of St Thomas.

intro: Today the Thirteen Days' Fast ends with the feast of the two pillars of the Church. Peter confesses Christ and receives the keys; Paul runs the race to the end. One was a fisherman, the other a persecutor. Christ made both apostles, and both were martyred in Rome.

points.h: Peter: the confession and the rock
sub: “Who do you say that I am?” Peter answers: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus names him Peter, the rock, and gives him the keys of the kingdom.
The Church rests on Christ and on the faith Peter confessed; Peter's ministry continues in the Bishop of Rome, with whom our Church is in full communion.
q: But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
points.apply: Pray today for Pope Leo XIV and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos.

sub: Peter denied the Lord three times; by the lake he is asked three times, “Do you love me?”
Each answer of love becomes a mission: “Feed my sheep.”
Authority in the Church is born of love and is exercised as shepherding, as God promised through Ezekiel.
q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.

He said to him the third time, “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Peter felt hurt because he said to him the third time, “Do you love me?” And he said to him, “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.”
points.apply: Where you have failed the Lord, tell him again simply: “Lord, you know that I love you.”

sub: Like Daniel, who resolved not to defile himself, Paul held firm.
From persecutor to apostle: grace changed his whole life's direction.
At the end he could say he had fought the good fight and kept the faith.
q: But Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the royal rations of food and wine; so he asked the palace master to allow him not to defile himself.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
points.apply: Choose one area of life where you need perseverance and offer it to God today.

concl: Different temperaments, one faith, one Lord, one martyrdom.
Like Peter and Paul, let us confess Christ, love him after our falls, and run to the end.
2027-06-29.resolve: Read Acts 12:6–19 with your family and pray for the Church's shepherds.

intro: Theme: “Rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
The Lord sends out the seventy: mission begins with prayer, travels light, serves the word and the table, and finds its joy in belonging to God.

points.h: Ask the Lord of the harvest
sub: Before any instruction, Jesus gives the seventy a prayer.
The harvest belongs to the Lord, and so do the labourers.
Every vocation in the Church begins with someone praying.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.”
points.apply: Each day this week pray for one priest, one religious and one young person who may be called.

sub: No purse, no bag, no sandals: the messenger carries little so the message is seen clearly.
Their first word in every house is peace.
Jericho fell by obedience and prayer, not by weapons.
q: And at the seventh time, when the priests had blown the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, “Shout! For the LORD has given you the city.”
Whatever house you enter, first say, “Peace to this house!”
points.apply: When you enter a home this week, bless it silently: Peace to this house.

points.h: Servants of the word and of the table
sub: The apostles choose seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom.
Prayer and the ministry of the word go together with service.
God preserves his servants as the vine-grower spares the cluster with a blessing in it.
q: Thus says the LORD: As the wine is found in the cluster, and they say, “Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it,” so I will do for my servants' sake, and not destroy them all.

Therefore, friends, select from among yourselves seven men of good standing, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint to this task, while we, for our part, will devote ourselves to prayer and to serving the word.
points.apply: Offer one hour of service to your parish this month: catechism, choir, the sick or the poor.

points.h: Rejoice that your names are written in heaven
sub: The seventy return rejoicing that even the demons submit.
Jesus points them to a deeper joy.
Success in ministry passes; belonging to God remains.
q: O LORD, who may abide in your tent? Who may dwell on your holy hill?
Nevertheless, do not rejoice at this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.
points.apply: Thank God tonight that he knows you by name.

concl: The harvest is the Lord's; pray, go in peace, and serve.
Our deepest joy is that God has written our names in heaven.
2027-06-13.resolve: Prepare now for the Apostles' Fast from 16 June: daily prayer for vocations and for the Church's mission.
